title: Advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction

notes.definition: Sexual reproduction produces variation in the offspring, which helps a species survive when the environment changes. Asexual reproduction needs only one parent and is faster and more efficient, producing many identical offspring when conditions are favourable. Some organisms use both methods.
explanation: The main advantage of sexual reproduction is that it produces variation in the offspring. Because genetic information from two parents is mixed, each offspring has a different combination of alleles. If the environment changes, for example a new disease appears or the climate becomes colder, some individuals may by chance have characteristics that help them survive. These individuals are more likely to survive and breed, passing on their alleles. This is natural selection, so variation gives a species a survival advantage.

Humans can speed up the effect of natural selection by selective breeding. Breeders choose parents with useful characteristics and breed them together, relying on sexual reproduction to combine features. This has been used to increase food production, for example by breeding crops with higher yields or cattle that produce more milk.

Sexual reproduction also has disadvantages. Two parents are needed, so an organism has to find a mate, which takes time and energy (in plants, pollination may depend on wind or insects). It is slower than asexual reproduction and produces fewer offspring. Any useful combination of alleles in a successful parent may be broken up in the offspring.

Asexual reproduction has several advantages. Only one parent is needed. It is more time and energy efficient because the organism does not need to find a mate. It is faster than sexual reproduction, and many identical offspring can be produced when conditions are favourable, so a well suited organism can quickly colonise a good habitat. The main disadvantage is the lack of variation: if the environment changes or a disease appears, all the offspring are equally vulnerable and the whole population could be wiped out.

Some organisms can reproduce by both methods depending on the circumstances. Malarial parasites reproduce asexually in the human host but sexually in the mosquito. Many fungi reproduce asexually by spores but also reproduce sexually to give variation. Many plants produce seeds by sexual reproduction, but also reproduce asexually by runners (such as strawberry plants) or by bulb division (such as daffodils). Using both methods gives the benefits of rapid reproduction when conditions are good and variation when conditions change.
keyFacts: Sexual reproduction produces variation in the offspring.
Variation gives a survival advantage by natural selection if the environment changes.
Humans speed up natural selection by selective breeding to increase food production.
Asexual reproduction needs only one parent.
Asexual reproduction is more time and energy efficient as no mate is needed.
Asexual reproduction is faster than sexual reproduction.
Many identical offspring can be produced asexually when conditions are favourable.
Malarial parasites: asexual in the human host, sexual in the mosquito.
Fungi: asexual by spores, and sexual to give variation.
Plants: sexual by seeds; asexual by runners (strawberry) or bulb division (daffodil).

keyTerms.definition: Differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species.
The process by which individuals with characteristics best suited to the environment are more likely to survive and breed, passing on their alleles.
Humans choosing parents with desired characteristics to breed together, so the characteristics become more common in the offspring.
A small reproductive cell, for example released by fungi, that can grow into a new individual.
A stem that grows along the ground from a plant such as a strawberry and produces new plants asexually.
Asexual reproduction in plants such as daffodils, where a bulb divides to form new bulbs that each grow into a new plant.
The organism in which a parasite lives; for the malarial parasite, humans are a host.

workedExamples.title: Evaluating asexual reproduction for a crop
workedExamples.question: A farmer grows a field of genetically identical banana plants produced asexually. Give one advantage and one risk of this method.
steps: Advantage: identify what asexual reproduction gives. All the plants are clones of a good parent, so they all have the same desirable features, and many plants can be produced quickly.
Risk: identify what clones lack. There is no genetic variation.
Link the lack of variation to an environmental change: if a new disease arrives, no plant is likely to be resistant, so the whole crop could be destroyed.
workedExamples.answer: Advantage: plants are identical with the desired features and can be produced quickly from one parent. Risk: no variation, so a disease could kill all the plants.

workedExamples.title: Explaining why an organism uses both methods
workedExamples.question: Explain why it is an advantage for a fungus to reproduce asexually by spores in good conditions and sexually at other times.
steps: Asexual reproduction is fast and needs only one parent, so in favourable conditions the fungus can produce many spores and spread quickly.
If conditions change, some of the varied offspring may be better suited and survive (natural selection).
workedExamples.answer: Asexual reproduction allows rapid spread when conditions are good; sexual reproduction gives variation so some offspring can survive if conditions change.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think asexual reproduction is always worse than sexual reproduction.
misconceptions.right: In fact asexual reproduction is very successful in a stable environment: it is fast, needs only one parent and saves time and energy.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think organisms choose to change their genes when the environment changes.
misconceptions.right: In fact variation already exists in a population produced by sexual reproduction; the individuals that happen to be better suited survive and breed (natural selection).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think an organism can only reproduce in one way.
misconceptions.right: In fact malarial parasites, many fungi and many plants can reproduce both sexually and asexually depending on circumstances.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 'faster' is the only advantage of asexual reproduction.
misconceptions.right: In fact there are several: only one parent is needed, no time or energy is spent finding a mate, and many identical offspring can be produced when conditions are favourable.

realWorld: Most commercial bananas are clones. A fungal disease called Panama disease has destroyed large areas of banana plantations because there is no genetic variation to provide resistance.
Farmers have used selective breeding, which depends on sexual reproduction, to produce wheat with higher yields and cows that give more milk.
Strawberry growers propagate new plants from runners to get many plants with the same fruit quality as the parent.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic is in separate Biology only (not Combined Science Trilogy): the advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction.

Advantages of sexual reproduction: variation in offspring, giving a survival advantage by natural selection if the environment changes; natural selection can be speeded up by humans in selective breeding to increase food production.
Advantages of asexual reproduction: only one parent needed; more time and energy efficient as no mate is needed; faster; many identical offspring when conditions are favourable.

Organisms that use both: malarial parasites (asexual in human host, sexual in mosquito), many fungi (asexual by spores, sexual for variation), many plants (seeds sexually, runners or bulb division asexually).
examTips: In 'evaluate' questions give advantages and disadvantages of both types, then end with a justified conclusion linked to the situation in the question (stable or changing environment).
Always link variation to natural selection: 'variation means some individuals may survive if the environment changes'.
Learn the three examples of organisms that use both methods exactly as the specification states; you will not be asked about other organisms without information being given.
Avoid vague answers like 'it is quicker'. Say 'it is faster because no mate needs to be found, so many offspring can be produced quickly when conditions are favourable'.
summary: Sexual reproduction gives variation, which helps survival if the environment changes.
Humans use sexual reproduction in selective breeding to increase food production.
Asexual reproduction: one parent, no mate needed, faster, many identical offspring.
Asexual reproduction gives no variation, so a population is vulnerable to change or disease.
Malarial parasites, many fungi and many plants reproduce in both ways.
Using both methods gives speed in good conditions and variation when conditions change.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of sexual reproduction?
options: It produces variation in the offspring
markScheme: 1 mark: it produces variation in the offspring
questions.explanation: Mixing genetic information from two parents gives varied offspring. The other options are advantages or features of asexual reproduction.

questions.question: Which is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
markScheme: 1 mark: only one parent is needed
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction needs just one parent, so no time or energy is spent finding a mate. It does not produce variation.

questions.question: How do strawberry plants reproduce asexually?
markScheme: 1 mark: by runners
questions.explanation: Strawberries send out runners that grow into new plants. Daffodils use bulbs, fungi use spores, and seeds come from sexual reproduction.

questions.question: Where does the malarial parasite reproduce sexually?
markScheme: 1 mark: in the mosquito
questions.explanation: The malarial parasite reproduces asexually in the human host and sexually in the mosquito.

questions.question: Which plant reproduces asexually by bulb division?
markScheme: 1 mark: daffodil
questions.explanation: Daffodil bulbs divide to form new bulbs. Strawberries use runners.

questions.question: Why is asexual reproduction more time and energy efficient than sexual reproduction?
options: No mate needs to be found
Meiosis uses less energy than mitosis
markScheme: 1 mark: no mate needs to be found
questions.explanation: Finding and attracting a mate takes time and energy. Asexual reproduction avoids this. Asexual reproduction uses mitosis, not meiosis, and gives no variation.

questions.question: How do many fungi reproduce?
options: Asexually by spores, and also sexually to give variation
markScheme: 1 mark: asexually by spores, and also sexually to give variation
questions.explanation: Many fungi produce spores asexually but can also reproduce sexually, which produces variation.

questions.question: A population of aphids reproduces asexually all summer, then sexually in autumn before winter. What is the most likely advantage of reproducing sexually in autumn?
options: It is faster, so more aphids are produced before winter
It produces variation, so some offspring may survive the changing conditions
It means only one parent is needed
It produces clones that are all suited to winter
markScheme: 1 mark: it produces variation so some offspring may survive the changing conditions
questions.explanation: In summer conditions are favourable, so fast asexual reproduction makes many offspring. As conditions change, variation from sexual reproduction makes it more likely that some individuals will survive.

questions.question: A field of genetically identical potato plants is infected by a new disease. Every plant dies. What is the best explanation?
options: The plants had no genetic variation, so none had resistance
The disease caused mutations in every plant
The plants were produced by sexual reproduction
markScheme: 1 mark: no genetic variation, so none had resistance
questions.explanation: Clones share the same alleles, so if one plant is not resistant, none are. A sexually produced population would be more likely to contain some resistant individuals. Asexually produced plants are not inherently weaker.

questions.question: Which statement explains how variation from sexual reproduction leads to a survival advantage?
options: Organisms change their genes to suit a new environment
All offspring become better suited to the environment
Individuals with characteristics suited to the new environment are more likely to survive and breed, passing on their alleles
Variation stops the environment from changing
markScheme: 1 mark: suited individuals more likely to survive and breed and pass on alleles
questions.explanation: This is natural selection. Organisms cannot change their genes in response to the environment; the variation already exists and the environment 'selects' the best suited individuals.

questions.question: Give two advantages of asexual reproduction.
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two: only one parent needed; more time and energy efficient as no mate needed; faster than sexual reproduction; many identical offspring can be produced when conditions are favourable
questions.explanation: These four advantages are listed in the specification. 'Quicker' alone is acceptable as 'faster'.

questions.question: Name two types of organism that can reproduce both sexually and asexually.
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two: malarial parasite; fungi; plants (for example strawberries or daffodils)
questions.explanation: The specification examples are malarial parasites, many fungi and many plants.

questions.question: Give one disadvantage of sexual reproduction and one disadvantage of asexual reproduction.
acceptedAnswers: asexual population wiped out by disease or change
markScheme: 1 mark: sexual: two parents needed / time and energy to find a mate / slower / fewer offspring
1 mark: asexual: no variation, so a change in the environment or disease could kill all offspring
questions.explanation: The disadvantages are the reverse of the advantages: sexual is slow and needs a mate; asexual gives no variation.

questions.question: Describe how the malarial parasite uses both sexual and asexual reproduction.
markScheme: 1 mark: reproduces asexually in the human host
1 mark: reproduces sexually in the mosquito
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction in the human allows rapid multiplication of the parasite; sexual reproduction in the mosquito produces variation.

questions.question: Explain how humans can speed up natural selection to increase food production.
markScheme: 1 mark: selective breeding
1 mark: choosing parents with desired characteristics (for example high yield) and breeding them together (over many generations)
questions.explanation: Selective breeding is artificial selection. Humans decide which individuals breed, so desired characteristics become common much faster than by natural selection.

questions.question: Explain why reproducing asexually is an advantage to a plant growing in a stable environment where it is well suited.
markScheme: 1 mark: offspring are genetically identical (clones) so inherit all the characteristics that make the parent well suited
1 mark: reproduction is faster / many offspring produced quickly when conditions are favourable
1 mark: no need to find a mate (or rely on pollinators), so more time and energy efficient
questions.explanation: In a stable environment there is little benefit to variation. Producing many clones of a well suited parent quickly lets the plant colonise the area.

questions.question: A farmer has a herd of cows that all came from one cow by cloning. Suggest one reason this could be a problem if a new disease appears.
markScheme: 1 mark: the cows have no genetic variation / identical alleles
1 mark: so if one is not resistant, none are and the whole herd could be killed
questions.explanation: Clones all respond to a disease in the same way. Variation increases the chance that some individuals survive.

questions.question: Name the process, used by humans, that speeds up natural selection to increase food production.
markScheme: 1 mark: selective breeding (accept artificial selection)
questions.explanation: Selective breeding uses sexual reproduction between chosen parents.

questions.question: Many plants can reproduce sexually by producing seeds and asexually, for example by runners or bulbs. Explain the advantages to a plant of being able to reproduce in both ways.
markScheme: Indicative content: asexual (runners or bulbs) needs only one parent, no pollination or mate needed, faster, time and energy efficient, many identical offspring when conditions are favourable, offspring keep parent's well suited characteristics; sexual (seeds) produces variation, if the environment changes some offspring may be suited and survive (natural selection); seeds can also be dispersed to new areas; using both gives the plant rapid reproduction in good conditions and variation for changing conditions.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear explanation of at least one advantage of each type, linked to conditions (favourable or changing).
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements of advantages of one or both types without linking to conditions.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that each method suits different circumstances: asexual for speed when conditions are good, sexual for variation when conditions change.

questions.question: Evaluate the use of sexual reproduction and asexual reproduction for a species living in an environment that changes often. Give a conclusion.
markScheme: Indicative content. Sexual advantages: mixing of genetic information gives variation; if the environment changes some individuals may have characteristics that help them survive; they breed and pass on alleles (natural selection); reduces chance of whole population dying from a disease. Sexual disadvantages: needs two parents; time and energy needed to find a mate; slower; fewer offspring. Asexual advantages: one parent; no mate needed so more time and energy efficient; faster; many identical offspring when conditions are favourable. Asexual disadvantages: no variation; all offspring equally vulnerable to environmental change or disease; whole population could be wiped out. Conclusion: in an often-changing environment sexual reproduction is likely to be more beneficial (or using both, as in fungi, plants and malarial parasites, gives speed in good periods and variation when conditions change), justified with reasons.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): a balanced evaluation of advantages and disadvantages of both types, linked to a changing environment, with a justified conclusion.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): advantages and disadvantages of both types given with some linking to the environment; conclusion may be missing or not justified.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): a few simple advantages or disadvantages, mostly of one type.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: An 'evaluate' question needs both sides and a judgement. The changing environment is the key context: variation is the deciding factor, although organisms that use both methods gain the benefits of each.

questions.question: Which row correctly matches the organism to its methods of reproduction?
options: Daffodil: sexual by spores, asexual by seeds
Strawberry: sexual by seeds, asexual by runners
Malarial parasite: sexual in the human, asexual in the mosquito
Fungi: sexual by runners, asexual by bulbs
markScheme: 1 mark: strawberry: sexual by seeds, asexual by runners
questions.explanation: Strawberry plants make seeds sexually and runners asexually. The malarial parasite row is reversed (asexual in human, sexual in mosquito). Fungi use spores, and daffodils use bulbs asexually.

questions.question: Explain why many identical offspring produced asexually can be an advantage when conditions are favourable.
acceptedAnswers: offspring identical and also well suited
markScheme: 1 mark: the offspring are identical to a parent that is well suited to the conditions
1 mark: many offspring can be produced quickly to use the resources / colonise the area
questions.explanation: When conditions are good, there is no need for variation; making many copies of a successful organism quickly is the best strategy.

questions.question: Scientists found that a species of snail reproduces mostly sexually in ponds with many parasites, but mostly asexually in ponds with few parasites. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Parasites cause snails to stop making gametes
Snails in ponds with few parasites cannot reproduce sexually
Asexual reproduction produces more variation than sexual reproduction
Sexual reproduction is favoured where variation helps offspring survive a changing threat
markScheme: 1 mark: sexual reproduction is favoured where variation helps offspring survive a changing threat
questions.explanation: Parasites keep changing, so variation increases the chance some offspring are resistant. Where there are few parasites, the speed of asexual reproduction is more useful. The data do not show that snails cannot reproduce sexually.

questions.question: State the main disadvantage of asexual reproduction.
markScheme: 1 mark: no variation (so the population may not survive a change in environment or a disease)
questions.explanation: Without variation, all offspring are equally affected by any change.

questions.question: Describe the different ways in which malarial parasites, fungi and plants reproduce.
markScheme: Indicative content: malarial parasites reproduce asexually in the human host and sexually in the mosquito; many fungi reproduce asexually by spores and also reproduce sexually to give variation; many plants reproduce sexually to produce seeds; plants also reproduce asexually by runners (strawberry) or bulb division (daffodil).
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct description of both methods for at least two of the organisms, including named plant examples.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correct methods given.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: These are the examples given in the specification and are commonly tested in short recall form or as part of longer answers.

questions.question: Which of these is a disadvantage of sexual reproduction?
options: It takes more time and energy because a mate must be found
markScheme: 1 mark: it takes more time and energy because a mate must be found
questions.explanation: Finding a mate takes time and energy. The other options describe asexual reproduction.
